We also expect to continue to incur additional expenses related to compliance and reporting obligations pursuant to the rules and regulations of the SEC and debt agreements, general insurance and directors’ and officers’ insurance, investor relations and other professional services.

While EV adoption is expected to continue to grow, the pace of that growth may be slower than previously anticipated, which could affect the near-term demand for our charging services and the rate at which we realize expected returns on our infrastructure investments.

If the market for EVs does not develop as expected or if there is any further slowdown or delay in overall adoption of EVs, our business, financial condition and results of operations may be materially and adversely affected.

As such, electrification of vehicle fleets may occur more slowly or more rapidly than management forecasts based on the cost to purchase, operate and maintain EVs and the general availability of such vehicles relative to those of internal combustion engine vehicles.

There is a risk that some or all of the components of the EV technology ecosystem will become obsolete and that we will be required to make significant investments to continue to effectively operate our business.
